item.title: Goshikidai Plateau: Scenic Heights over the Sea — Guide
item.description: Goshikidai is a broad lava plateau rising between Takamatsu and Sakaide on the Kagawa coast, its name (‘five-colour heights’) referring to five hills. A scenic road crosses the plateau, linking viewpoints, walking trails, a planetarium and quiet woodland, with sweeping panoramas over the Seto Inland Sea and its islands. From its western edge there are especially fine views of the great Seto Ohashi bridge striding across the water toward Honshu, magnificent at sunset and when lit at night.

item.title: Shikoku Karst: A Highland of Cattle and Sky — Guide
item.description: The Shikoku Karst is one of Japan’s three great karst plateaus, a striking highland running along the Ehime–Kochi border at around 1,400 metres. Here rolling green grassland stretches to the horizon, studded with weathered white limestone rocks and grazed by cattle in summer, under enormous open skies — a landscape utterly unlike the rest of mountainous Shikoku. A scenic skyline road runs along the plateau, passing viewpoints, a campground and windmills, with sweeping panoramas over range after range of Shikoku’s mountains.

item.title: Yashima: Flat-Topped Plateau and History — Guide
item.description: Yashima is a striking flat-topped lava plateau that rises steeply above the coast just east of Takamatsu, its level summit and sheer sides making it a local landmark. From the top, terraces and viewpoints command sweeping panoramas over Takamatsu, the island-dotted Seto Inland Sea, and the surrounding coast — especially beautiful at sunset. The plateau is steeped in history: it was the site of the Battle of Yashima in 1185, a famous clash of the Genpei War between the Minamoto and Taira clans, remembered in legend and place names.
